news.headline: Watson cleared and starting for CLE; Texans thin up front
news.detail: Deshaun Watson cleared concussion protocol and is set to start against HOU (reported Nov 11-13). The Texans will reportedly be without Danielle Hunter and Azeez Al-Shaair, and Marvin Harrison Jr. is also missing. Cleveland is also reported to have not allowed a 300-yard passer in 54 straight games. Fullback Michael Burton and safety Ronnie Hickman missed Friday practice. The sportsbooks still fav…

news.headline: Bills offensive line banged up before trip to Jets
news.detail: Spencer Brown (ankle) missed Thursday practice, and Dion Dawkins, Connor McGovern and Alec Anderson were limited (Nov 12-13 reports). The Jets rank 26th against the run, and James Cook ran 31 times for 107 yards last week. Jets WR Garrett Wilson is expected to clear concussion protocol.

news.headline: Brissett makes Ravens debut on a short week; Herbert healthy
news.detail: Jacoby Brissett was acquired Nov 6 and has had about four days of practice. Baltimore has lost four straight and has not scored more than 13 in any of them. Justin Herbert (finger) was not on the Chargers' injury report Nov 12. Ravens CB Nate Wiggins and safeties Kyle Hamilton and Jaylinn Hawkins are questionable.

news.headline: Rams without Nacua; Cardinals start rookie Carson Beck
news.detail: Puka Nacua is out and Davante Adams is on IR, so the Rams' receiver group is thin (Nov 10-13). Matthew Stafford was a full participant. Arizona starts rookie Carson Beck in his first game, with Gardner Minshew on IR and WR Michael Wilson out for the season. Center Hjalte Froholdt is in concussion protocol. TE Trey McBride is the clear top target.

news.headline: Lock limited but set to start for SEA; Smith-Njigba full
news.detail: Drew Lock (elbow, oblique) was limited both days but the team plans to start him; Sam Darnold is out. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had a rest day Wednesday and was full Thursday. LT Charles Cross was limited after missing two games. Guard Quenton Nelson and DT Leonard Williams did not practice. Raiders start rookie Fernando Mendoza.

news.headline: 49ers: Trent Williams, four CBs questionable; Evans out
news.detail: Trent Williams (shoulder) sat out Friday and is questionable. CBs Renardo Green, Nate Hobbs, Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout are also questionable, and Mike Evans (Achilles) is listed out. Deebo Samuel had a hamstring issue this week. Dallas CB Joey Porter Jr. was not ruled out. CeeDee Lamb has been targeted an NFL-high 108 times.

news.headline: Mahomes full all week; Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker questionable
news.detail: Patrick Mahomes (knee/right elbow) was a full participant all week, and Xavier Worthy was full too. Running back Kenneth Walker is questionable with a groin issue after missing Friday practice. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) missed practice Wednesday and Thursday.

news.headline: Bengals line intact for Steelers; Dugger out
news.detail: Per the Nov 13 final report, Bengals guard Dylan Fairchild is good to go despite a pec injury, so the same five starters protect Joe Burrow. Safety Kyle Dugger will miss the game. WR Andrei Iosivas was cleared to return to practice this week.

NFL.recap: Weeks 9 and 10 went well for picking winners and totals but poorly against the spread. The model picked 14 of 16 winners; the misses were WAS over NYG and GB over NE, where NE had four turnovers. It went 7-9 against the spread and 10-4 on over/unders. Several big misses came from finishing drives, turnovers and efficiency, which are hard to see before kickoff: JAX-BAL was off by 17.5 and HOU-LAC by 18.1.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, its side wins about as often as Vegas's chances say, which is less than half the time.
lessons.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games this season where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won. Past-season test: the model's side won 47.4% in 2010-2019 (Vegas 42.9%) and 42.9% in 2020-2025 (Vegas 43.3%), so no edge over Vegas's own chances. HOU at CLE is this week's case.
lessons.test: Check results of the attached check on 2010-2019 and 2020-2025 against Vegas's chances; add up this season's cases until there are 20+.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.

lessons.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
lessons.evidence: Past-season test says the model's side with a 4+ point gap won 48.3% in 2020-2025 (174 games, 4 pushes), below break-even; no 2010-2019 data. This season, the over/under is 30-24 overall and went 10-4 in the last two weeks, so the small sample does not show the same weakness. L9 (gap 5.3) fits this group.
lessons.test: Compare gap groups under 2, 2-4 and 4+ on past seasons; keep tracking this season's 4+ gap games until 20+.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.

lessons.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
lessons.evidence: 9 of the 16 games where the winner was wrong through Week 9 named efficiency as the main reason (not updated for the WAS-NYG miss, which had no named driver). Newest misses: JAX-BAL off by 17.5 and HOU-LAC by 18.1, with no stat explaining most of it.
lessons.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

lessons.lesson: Long-shot picks (underdog winners and big-game props) hit a bit below the model's chances and lose units.
lessons.evidence: Underdog picks are 5 of 19 against 7.7 expected (-6.54 units). Big-game picks are 12 of 36 against 11.8 expected (-8.99 units), so the loss is mostly from prices. Milestone picks are 31 of 40 against 29.9 expected (-3.29 units).
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for underdog winners and long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running a little below the model's chances.
lessons.evidence: 12 of 24 best-value picks hit this season, against 12.7 expected, at -1.09 units. The gap is under 1 hit. This week's five value picks sit only 0.4 to 1.0 points over break-even.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks per edge group.

lessons.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
lessons.evidence: Average spread miss is 9.7 for the model vs 9.0 for Vegas over 56 graded games; the model is 25-31-1 against the spread (7-9 in the last two weeks). Past-season test of the model's spread side: 51.9% in 2010-2019 and 48.9% in 2020-2025 across 1,660 games. That is below the 52.4% break-even, so no edge.
lessons.test: Compare average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week and season, before changing anything.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.

lessons.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas on games with a QB change are not clearly misses by the model.
lessons.evidence: Earlier cases: DAL at PHI, PHI at WAS (Hurts on IR) and MIN (Murray out, Wentz in). Past-season test of the model's spread side with a QB change and a 3+ point gap: 54.2% in 2010-2019 (203 games) and 54.4% in 2020-2025 (160 games). That is above break-even but short of the 54.5% needed to count as an edge. This week BAL, ARI, MIA, SEA, LV and CLE have QB changes.
lessons.test: Track this season's cases until 20+; compare the model's margin error in QB-change games with all others.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.

lessons.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen a little short of the model's chances, but this looks like luck.
lessons.evidence: 16 of 24 hit this season vs 17.4 expected (-3.27 units). Past-season test: the model's side at 70%+ when it agrees with Vegas won 80.4% in 2010-2019 (Vegas 77.1%) and 77.8% in 2020-2025 (Vegas 77.1%), so about what Vegas's chances said. The 1.4-hit shortfall is within normal swings, so this lesson is retired.
lessons.test: No further test needed unless the shortfall grows past 20+ picks per bucket.

test_result.note: No game history from this run.

news.headline: ASU-UCF kickoff moved to 5:30 PM after travel delay; UCF thin
news.detail: Arizona State's charter was held up by a national ground stoppage, so the game was pushed back (Nov 14). UCF is also without RB Duke Watson and three defensive backs, and QB Keyone Jenkins is questionable, though Alonza Barnett III is back as starter.

news.headline: ASU starts a true freshman QB, Jake Fette, on the road
news.detail: Fette has started Arizona State's last two games after Mikey Keene hurt his knee. Keene is available as a backup. A late flight and a young QB are things the model can't see.

news.headline: Ole Miss QB Chambliss cleared, but Rebels are banged up
news.detail: Trinidad Chambliss was dropped from the SEC report after a Wednesday 'probable' tag, so he is expected to start (Nov 12-13). RB Kewan Lacy, OL Patrick Kutas and LB Keaton Thomas are out, and RB Makhi Frazier is questionable. Oklahoma has five players out. This is a model-vs-Vegas disagreement: the model has Ole Miss, Vegas has Oklahoma.

news.headline: App State-Marshall: no QB news; both lines hurt
news.detail: Marshall is without left tackle Tariq Montgomery and App State has lost three starting linemen, per Nov 12 previews. The home team has won the last six meetings. No sign of a QB change on either side. This is a model-vs-Vegas disagreement: the model has Marshall, Vegas has App State.

news.headline: Georgia center Drew Bobo questionable vs. Missouri
news.detail: Bobo, who has started every game at center, was added to the SEC report as questionable on Thursday (Nov 12-13). DT Joshua Horton is also questionable and OLB Amaris Williams is out. Otherwise Georgia is healthy.

news.headline: Texas Tech short at receiver and RB for Oklahoma State
news.detail: Texas Tech WR Coy Eakin (broken hand) and RB Quinten Joyner are out; RB Cam Dickey is probable on an ankle. Oklahoma State is missing LB Tate Romney and several depth players (Nov 13-14).

news.headline: Texas WR Cam Coleman back at LSU, but not at full strength
news.detail: Coleman is off the injury report after missing the Missouri game, but a report says he aggravated a shoulder injury and practiced in a non-contact jersey (Nov 13). LSU lists LB Whit Weeks as questionable. Arch Manning has been sacked 27 times this season.

news.headline: Iowa without OL Cael Winter; Purdue fired its defensive coordinator
news.detail: Iowa's Cael Winter is not expected to play and RB Kamari Moulton is out for the season (Nov 11-13). Purdue fired defensive coordinator Kevin Kane earlier this week. QB Hank Brown is listed as Iowa's starter.

news.headline: Tulane's QB situation unsettled at Rice
news.detail: A Tulane preview (Nov 14) says Trace Johnson or Dagan Bruno will play QB, and that Zeon Chriss-Gremillion may not play again. Rice, 1-8, is favored only for the second time this year and has Gael Ochoa at QB.

College.recap: Week 11 results so far went well on winners and badly against the spread. The model picked 8 of 11 winners right, but was 1-10 against the spread. Houston, UCLA, Pittsburgh and Bowling Green were favored by the model by more than Vegas, and all four failed to cover. Over/under was 6-4 with one no pick. Week 10 reviews again put efficiency first in most big misses (Wyoming, Texas State, Utah State, Oklahoma).

lessons.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up, and the model's totals picks overall have lost more than they won.
lessons.evidence: Weeks 8-10: over hit in about 16 of 39 such games (41%). Season totals picks are 111-129 (46%). The 11 Week 11 results shown went 6-4 on totals picks (Louisiana had no pick), a better week but a small sample.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Also compare the model's and Vegas's average total error. Need 20+ games per group.

test_result.note: Won 51.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Big misses are spread across several causes, but efficiency still leads.
lessons.evidence: Week 10, 26 of the 40 results shown missed by 8+ points: efficiency first in 14, finishing drives 5, turnovers 4, nothing stood out 2, defensive/return touchdowns 1. Week 9 had efficiency first in 7 of 26; Week 8 in 15 of 25. Week 11 results still had no reviews. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin, defensive/return touchdowns and points per trip inside the 40 with long-run averages, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than Vegas, this season has gone badly, but past seasons say the model's side holds up.
lessons.evidence: This season about 4 of 14 right, with no new graded games since last run (Ohio-Miami (OH) and Western Kentucky-Middle Tennessee both went to Vegas). Three such games this week (Arizona State at UCF, Ole Miss at Oklahoma, App State at Marshall). Built-in test: the model's side won 47% in 2020-2025 against Vegas's 41%, but that test could not run this time.
lessons.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

test_result.note: Won 47% in 2020–2025 when Vegas's chances said 41%. Those chances have the bookmaker's cut removed; a real bet pays it, which eats a couple of points of that edge.

lessons.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak.
lessons.evidence: Season: 12 of 30 hit against 15.3 expected, at -7.09 units. No new results since last run. Edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed), so the model's own chance is below break-even on all five picks this week. Purdue +17.5 sits against the model's own Iowa by 26.6.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Underdog picks have hit a bit less often than the model expected, but long prices have kept units positive.
lessons.evidence: Season: 10 of 29 hit against 11.5 expected, at +1.56 units. No new underdog results since last run. A few hits swing the units a lot, so there is much luck in this list.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%, 45%+). Need 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: Season: 23 of 25 hit against 22.4 expected, at +0.49 units. No new results since last run. Prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The model's spread misses are slightly larger than Vegas's over the season, and favorites have covered a lot lately.
lessons.evidence: Season (245 games): average spread miss 12.4 for the model against 11.8 for Vegas. Winners right 162 of 245 (66.1%), spread record 112-127-4. In the 11 Week 11 results shown the model was 1-10 against the spread and the Vegas favorite covered in 7 of 11 (Houston, UCLA, Pittsburgh and Bowling Green favorites did not).
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, whether the gap changes by week of season, and whether favorites cover more often in November.

test_result.note: Won 50.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: When the model's margin for a favorite is 3+ points bigger than Vegas's, the recent record is mixed, and the newest games went against it.
lessons.evidence: By my count, about 9 of 14 such games covered in Weeks 10-11 earlier (Toledo, Liberty, Louisville, Jacksonville State, Boise State, North Texas, UAB, Wake Forest, Arizona State). The rest of Week 11 adds Houston, UCLA and Bowling Green as misses and Toledo as a hit, so roughly 10 of 18 overall. Under 20 games. Several games this week fit (Iowa, Liberty, Air Force, Georgia).
lessons.test: On past seasons, take games where the model's margin for the favorite exceeds Vegas's by 3+ and check how often the favorite covers, split by size of spread and by week. Need 20+ games per group.

test_result.note: Won 48.5% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.
